question: Do frozen AHA heads offer public temporal information conditional on a TRAIN-only cubic position model, or is denominator/calibration responsible for useful information being discarded?
hypothesis: If AHA contains transferable information beyond position, position+heads should beat position alone under exact matched85 budgets; if simple probability/count calibration is the missing mechanism, TRAIN-only plugin should improve its fixed85 decoder and beat position at its own K.
alternative: Generic-query AHA heads and their available observation/target contract do not encode transferable summary utility; changing a denominator cannot repair this.
models: Three source-macro logistic models: cubic normalized position, informativeness+relevance, and both. Fixed L2 ridge1e-3; no DEV selection. Native 1fps heads broadcast by nearest actual sampled PTS. Fit all TRAIN frames with each source weight1/26.
independent_unit: original source video; ten annotators averaged within source before macro mean and source-paired bootstrap
practical_gate: For the primary content-increment contrast, DEV macro delta>=0.005 and paired source-bootstrap95% interval lower bound>0. Gate reflects needing a nontrivial public diagnostic signal before more expensive semantic inference; not an official-score effect threshold.
resource: CPU only; timeout30m; no encoder training, GPU or official/protected data
stop: Axis/hash/PTS/source mismatch, NaN/Inf, nonconvergence, control disagreement with R26 at1e-12, or timeout. Preserve failure; no DEV retuning.
scope: Exposed public VideoXum temporal mechanism diagnostic; not official joint score
limitations: 14 DEV sources already exposed in R24/R26; no independent confirmation claim
VideoXum shortened-summary annotation policy differs from generic excitingness and AIC
No crop GT and no official score inference
The plugin uses an expected-numerator/expected-denominator approximation, not an exact posterior Bayes decision
Position conditioning is limited to this fixed cubic specification; no universal content-causality claim
GT-assisted diagnostics are nondeployable and use full GT unavailable to the actual input
GT block-mean broadcast is one feasible diagnostic recipe, not an upper bound on input learnability
Annotation-positive runs are not assumed to be physical events
The practical gate is a resource allocation criterion; its numerical choice is not a statistical law
